page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Own every preference this scenario needs: appearance, locale, accessibility, notification relay, retention, and the dependency status that explains system-wide behaviour.

priorities.statement: Theme and locale switching are owned here, per the shell contract.
Accessibility preferences (reduced motion, font scale) are first-class controls, not buried under an advanced section.
Relay configuration states plainly what happens when it is absent: handoffs still queue and nothing is lost.
Dependency status is visible here, including that act-as fails closed when the verification authority is unreachable.
priorities.notes: This is where an operator confirms why the whole scenario is refusing.

priorities.statement: Retention windows are shown as the product's real commitments, not as tunable knobs that would silently break the journal's append-only guarantee.

states.description: A change was saved, confirmed in place.
A submitted value was rejected, with the reason stated on the field.
One or more optional dependencies are unavailable; each is named with its consequence.
Dependency status is cached and may not reflect the current state; the age is stated.
Core settings load but optional dependency status cannot be resolved; each unresolved item is named.
A fresh install before any optional dependency or relay has been configured — defaults are shown as deliberate choices, not as missing values.
